# Summary

From React Native 0.88, an iOS app can use Swift Package Manager
(SwiftPM) in place of CocoaPods. A library takes part in that build when
it ships its own `Package.swift`. react-native-svg has none today, so a
SwiftPM app cannot use it.

This PR adds that support. CocoaPods behavior does not change.

Changes:
1. `Package.swift` with one library product, `RNSVG`. It targets iOS
15.1 and defines `RCT_NEW_ARCH_ENABLED=1`, as
`install_modules_dependencies` does under CocoaPods. React Native's
autolinker resolves the React Native packages it depends on.
2. `package.json`: `"swiftpmConfig": { "name": "RNSVG" }`. React Native
0.88 reads this name to link the product.
3. `#import <Foundation/Foundation.h>` in 7 headers that use Foundation
types without importing it. CocoaPods hid this through its prefix
header. SwiftPM has no prefix header.
4. `__tests__/swiftpm.test.ts` checks the manifest against the package:
product name, sources, header paths, defines, and that
`swiftpmConfig.name` matches the product.

The peer dependency on `react-native` does not change. SwiftPM mode
needs React Native 0.88 or newer. React Native 0.87 does not read
`swiftpmConfig.name`.

A follow-up PR ships the Metal filter kernels as SwiftPM resources.
Without it, `feComposite` with `operator="arithmetic"` or
`operator="xor"` draws nothing in a SwiftPM app. Every other element
works with this PR alone.

## Test Plan

### What's required for testing (prerequisites)?

- Xcode with an iOS simulator.
- A React Native 0.88.0 app: `npx @react-native-community/cli@latest
init SpmSvg088 --version 0.88.0`.

### What are the steps to reproduce (after prerequisites)?

1. Install this branch in the app. With a git install, set
`PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1`, because the `prepare` step otherwise
downloads a browser.
2. Switch the app to SwiftPM: `npx react-native spm add --deintegrate`.
The sync prints `Self-managed: RNSVG → ../node_modules/react-native-svg
(using its own Package.swift)`.
3. Render a screen with a circle, a rect and text.
4. Build Release for the simulator and run it.

Result on iPhone 18 Pro, iOS 27.0: BUILD SUCCEEDED, no SwiftPM warnings
for react-native-svg, and the shapes and text draw correctly.

Manifest test: `yarn jest __tests__/swiftpm.test.ts` passes, 7 of 7.

## Compatibility

| OS      | Implemented |
| ------- | :---------: |
| iOS     |    ✅      |
| MacOS   |    ❌      |
| Android |    ❌      |
| Web     |    ❌      |

SwiftPM mode is iOS only. CocoaPods builds on all platforms do not
change.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have tested this on a device and a simulator (tested on the
simulator only)
- [ ] I added documentation in `README.md`
- [ ] I updated the typed files (typescript)
